caption: A garden sprayer mists water onto a bare branch in deep winter cold, and the mist freezes into a white glaze on the twigs within seconds.

sa.check: A sprayer mists water onto a bare branch.
The wet twigs turn white and glassy.
The glaze thickens with more spraying.
Drops on the twigs stop running and hang as ice.
The setting reads as deep winter cold.
The spraying comes first and the glaze follows.

pc.expect: The mist lands as fine drops that stop moving and become a hard glassy coat on the twigs, and the twigs stay rigid.
pc.fail: The drops stay runny and keep dripping off in the cold; or the glaze stays a soft slush that smears; or the twigs droop and swing like rope under a thin glaze; or the glaze sets as a dry white powder that blows away.

pc.expect: The glaze only thickens with more spraying and does not melt off while the cold holds.
pc.fail: The glaze melts off the twigs while the cold holds and nothing warms them; or the glaze thins between sprays; or the glaze forms and clears in turn; or the twigs are glazed before any mist reaches them.

pc.expect: The mist falls and drifts downward onto the twigs, drops hang from their undersides and any that fall go down.
pc.fail: The mist rises from the sprayer and gathers above the branch; or the drops on the twigs hang upward from their tops; or a drop leaves a twig and rises; or a fallen drop returns to a twig.

pc.expect: The glaze forms where the mist lands and twigs the mist misses stay bare.
pc.fail: A twig the mist never reached is glazed; or the mist lands on a twig and it stays bare and dry to the end of the clip; or the whole branch glazes at once while the mist plays on one part.

pc.expect: One branch and one sprayer; the ice on the twigs is the water that was sprayed.
pc.fail: Ice appears on a twig with no mist reaching it; or the glaze vanishes at a stroke; or a twig vanishes; or a second branch appears.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The branch's bark away from the glaze, the sprayer and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The bark changes colour; or the sprayer changes shape; or the background changes between frames.
